dial.summary: TOTAL crypto stable at ~$2.98T with BTC.D firm at 56.71% and BTC around $84,464; global M2 expanded to $103.66T (August 2026 G4 aggregate) while near-zero perp funding (0.0095%) confirms unlevered spot accumulation, sustaining the BTC Accumulation posture despite DXY pushing to 101.11 (headwind) and real yields holding at 2.85% ahead of the October 1 ISM and October 2 NFP catalysts.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at approximately $103.66T as of August 2026 per MacroMicro (6–8 week reporting lag); US M2 at $23.3T in August 2026 (+5.7% YoY); 4-week trend up: ~$103.0T (late August) → $103.66T (latest August observation) = +0.6% over 4 weeks, meeting the supportive threshold; status supportive (4-week rising trend confirmed); September ISM (Oct 1) and September NFP (Oct 2) are next major macro catalysts that could affect the forward M2 outlook.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1); September ISM Manufacturing releases October 1 — no new official ISM reading as of September 28; LEADING SIGNAL: S&P Global Flash US Manufacturing PMI for September surged to 57.0 (52-month high, released Sep 23) pointing to potential ISM upside on Oct 1; 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → Aug 54.6% = −1.0pp on latest available official data; status neutral (ISM above 50 but falling on 4-week basis; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 or above 62 — neither applies); a Sep ISM print above 55 and rising on Oct 1 would shift status to supportive.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at ~101.11 on September 28, 2026 (held near 101 through the week, closing the week in a firm range; Sep 27 close also above 101 per Vietnam.vn/Vantage Markets); 4-week trend up: ~99.60 (Aug 26 per Barchart) → 101.11 (Sep 28) = +1.5% over 4 weeks, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind — DXY remains above the 100 threshold; hawkish Fed stance (fed funds 3.75%–4.00% post Sep 16 hike) and elevated real yields (2.85%) continue to underpin USD strength; a sustained official close below 100 is required to return to neutral status; trend derivation consistent with 30-day DTWEXBGS broad dollar index movement.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.85% as of September 25, 2026 (last available weekday reading; Sep 28 is Sunday — no new FRED observation); breakeven inflation rate near 2.28%; 10Y nominal 5.21% on Sep 28; 4-week trend up: ~2.47% (Aug 28) → 2.85% (Sep 25) = +38bps; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met); next DFII10 observation expected Monday Sep 29; a sustained fall below 2% required to shift status to neutral/supportive.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 28, 2026: 10Y Treasury at 5.21%, 2Y at 4.87% → 2s10s spread = +0.34% (+34bps); 4-week trend flat: ~+38bps (Aug 26, pre-FOMC range) → +34bps (Sep 28) = −4bps over 4 weeks, within the <5bps flat threshold; status neutral (positive spread but not steepening on 4-week basis; supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening; deeply inverted < −50bps for headwind does not apply); October 27–28 FOMC is the next major repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,747,704M ($6.75T) for week ending September 23, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released September 24 (Treasuries $4,558B, MBS $1,910B, other $279B); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.734T (Aug 26 estimate) → $6.748T (Sep 23) = +$14B over ~4 weeks, marginal expansion within flat range; total assets up ~$140B year-on-year; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no change to QT pace announced at Sep 16 FOMC); next H.4.1 release expected Thursday Oct 2.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at ~0.0095% per 8h (latest available per MacroMicro/CoinGlass; CoinGlass real-time access unavailable in this session); TOTAL crypto stable at ~$2.98T, BTC around $84,464, BTC.D at 56.71%; 30-day range consistently sub-0.01% throughout September; near-zero funding confirms the market is spot-driven and unlevered — a classic BTC accumulation signal; status supportive (well below the 0.04% overheating threshold); Oct 1 ISM and Oct 2 NFP are next potential catalysts for a funding regime change.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$309B as of late September 2026 (USDT ~$184B/59.5%, USDC ~$75B/24.3%; confirmed by multiple sources including StablecoinBeat and CoinGecko data); total crypto market cap ~$2.98T; stablecoin dominance ~10.36% (~$309B / $2.98T); 30-day trend down: dominance was ~10.5–11.0% in late August, falling to ~10.4% by late September as TOTAL held steady; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising dominance while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply); BTC.D 56.71%, holding firm above the 55% alt-rotation threshold.

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — forward-looking consumer sentiment after September's global central bank tightening cluster (Fed +25bps Sep 16, BOJ +25bps Sep 18); real yields at 2.85% and DXY at 101.11 remain headwinds for consumer psychology; a sharp decline from August would confirm elevated financing costs are weighing on demand; August PCE and Q2 GDP third estimate follow the next day on September 30.

upcoming.title: JOLTS Job Openings (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Bureau of Labor Statistics Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — key Fed input for assessing labor market tightness; a significant decline toward 7M openings would signal elevated rates are cooling labor demand; October 27–28 FOMC will weigh this alongside August PCE (Sep 30), September NFP (Oct 2), and FOMC Minutes (Oct 7).

upcoming.title: Q2 2026 GDP (Third Estimate)
upcoming.note: Bureau of Economic Analysis Q2 2026 GDP third (final) estimate at 8:30 AM ET — released alongside August PCE and ADP; a downward revision would add to recession concerns given the FOMC's hawkish Sep 16 hike and real yields at 2.85%; a strong final print would confirm the economy can absorb the current rate cycle, consistent with S&P Global Flash composite PMI 58.4 (5-year high) on September 23.

upcoming.title: PCE Price Index (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA Personal Income and Outlays report including August 2026 PCE Price Index at 8:30 AM ET — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge; July 2026 PCE was +3.7% YoY; a reading above +3.5% YoY reinforces the FOMC's case for continued tightening ahead of October 27–28; core PCE (ex food and energy) watched most closely; the last major inflation print before the October FOMC blackout period begins.

upcoming.title: ADP National Employment Report (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ADP Research Institute private payrolls estimate for September 2026 at 8:15 AM ET — advance read on labor conditions ahead of official NFP (Oct 2); released alongside Q2 GDP and August PCE on a data-dense final day of September; a strong print (+150K or above) reinforces the NFP-resilient narrative and keeps rate-hike expectations elevated for the October 27–28 FOMC.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Manufacturing PMI for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — most consequential ISM read in months; August ISM was 54.6%; S&P Global Flash Manufacturing PMI surged to 57.0 (52-month high) on September 23 — a strong leading signal; a print above 55 and rising would shift the ISM indicator to supportive status; a move below 50 would signal contraction and support a shift toward Risk Off posture.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 26, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 26, 2026 — released same day as ISM Manufacturing PMI; a back-to-back rise in claims would be an early signal that cumulative rate tightening (fed funds 3.75%–4.00%) is beginning to bite on employment; prior weeks approximately 206K.

upcoming.title: Employment Situation — September 2026 NFP
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET (first Friday of October) — the most consequential pre-FOMC data release before the October 27–28 meeting; August NFP was +162K; a reading above +200K with unemployment holding sub-4.5% keeps October hike odds elevated; a surprise miss below +100K could shift the rate path significantly; watch average hourly earnings for wage inflation signals.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Services PMI for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET (first Monday of October) — the services sector accounts for ~80% of US GDP; released after post-NFP market positioning from October 2 employment data; S&P Global Flash Services PMI for September surged to 58.7 (59-month high) on September 23 — a strong leading signal for ISM Services; a print below 50 alongside a soft NFP would significantly alter the rate-path outlook ahead of October 27–28 FOMC.
